prompts.name: Order sheet
Guided review
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one high-fidelity design concept for ShopBot called guided item review. This is a DIFFERENT interaction structure from a dense table: a small hardware shop owner sees ONE unresolved purchase decision at a time while the confirmed order stays visible. Single straight-on desktop screen landscape 1536x1024. Synthetic concept values. White, cool gray #F4F6F8, ShopBot blue #2563EB, dark #20252B, amber only for uncertainty. Readable sans-serif working labels and large touch-friendly buttons, subtle 4px corners, very restrained borders, no gradients, no decorative KPI cards.
Slim app sidebar 160px: ShopBot, Orders selected, Stock, Products, Conversations. Main header 'Order #8C1CE' and quiet link 'Back to orders'. Compact quiet text '2 items need your help'. Do NOT show a forced three-step generic wizard or pricing/payment/packing stages together.
Main work area is a large focused white panel titled exactly 'Which switch did the customer mean?' Above it a quote block 'Customer asked: 2 switches'. A subtle source link 'Read original message'. Then a catalog search labeled 'Find the right product'. Three horizontal product choice rows, each with a small accurate electrical switch thumbnail, name, price and unit:
'Anchor Roma 6A 1 Way' / '₹35 per piece' / button 'Use this switch';
'Anchor Roma 16A 1 Way' / '₹65 per piece' / button 'Use this switch';
'Anchor Penta 6A 1 Way' / '₹28 per piece' / button 'Use this switch'.
Below is a small text alternative 'Item is not in the catalog' which enables quoting a manual item; do not add an unrelated verification checklist. At the bottom of this work panel, small text 'Next: enter the pipe cutter price'. Selecting one product preserves requested quantity and fills verified selling facts, but does not send or reserve stock.
A calm narrow right panel is a read-only 'Order so far' list of eight product lines, not an editable spreadsheet: PVC Pipe 1 inch x2, switch x2 with amber Needs choice, PTFE tape x2, Pipe clamp x4, M-Seal 90g x1, PVC pipe cutter x1 with amber Needs price, Measuring tape 5m x1, Safety gloves x1. Footer '6 items ready' and 'Priced subtotal ₹808' with note '2 items not included'. Right panel is context only, no competing save/send/payment buttons. The main panel should be the clear focal point and use space intentionally. Show tiny note bottom 'Complete orders skip item review'. All copy concise and literal. Essential choices visibly named, no three-dot menus. This should feel easy for first-time shop staff and adaptable to a phone, without hiding the current order context. No decorative phone mockup, no marketing poster, just one clear realistic app interface.

prompts.name: Stock tasks
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a highly usable ShopBot inventory/stock task page, straight-on desktop app screenshot concept in landscape 1536x1024, intended for a small Indian hardware shop owner who simply needs to receive 6 pieces of stock. This page must feel dramatically simpler than a product editor or enterprise ERP. Match ShopBot blue #2563EB actions, white surfaces, cool #F4F6F8 page, dark #20252B, clean readable sans-serif 14-16px body equivalent and minimal 4px corners. Illustrative synthetic data, no gradients, no charts, no large KPI tiles, no unrelated product publishing fields.
Slim left sidebar ShopBot, Orders, Stock selected, Products, Conversations. Main heading 'Stock'. Small helper 'Find a product. Record what changed.' A prominent search input 'Search product, Tamil name or SKU'. Below it a clean stock table about 65% of content width with columns Product, On shelf, Held for orders, Available. Six representative hardware rows. The selected row 'PVC Pipe 1 inch' with small pipe photo shows exactly 12, 3, 9. Other rows: PTFE tape 24,4,20; Pipe clamp 36,8,28; M-Seal 90g 8,2,6; PVC pipe cutter 4,1,3; Safety gloves —,0,— with clear 'Stock not counted'. The held quantity is readable and never an editable number field. Small context 'Held quantities come from accepted orders.'
On the right, a focused task drawer about 35% width titled 'PVC Pipe 1 inch', small unit 'Sold per piece', small photo. Three visible task choices arranged as a short vertical or horizontal control: 'Receive stock' selected, 'Walk-in sale', 'Correct count'. Under selected mode show one prominent field labeled exactly 'How many pieces arrived?' with value '6' and pieces suffix. Optional smaller field 'Receipt or note (optional)'. Then a plain compact preview table labeled 'After saving': rows 'On shelf' 12 → 18, 'Held for orders' 3 → 3, 'Available' 9 → 15. A single dominant full-width blue button 'Save 6 received', quiet 'Cancel' link below. Show no price editor, no name/unit/brand publishing form, no generic action dropdown, no long mandatory reason text, no stock check checkbox. No pending order is fulfilled or paid by this action. The screen clearly distinguishes the item search/list from the currently selected simple stock task. Make literal labels crisp and legible with correct arithmetic. Shipping-quality UI proposal, not an infographic or moodboard.

edit.name: Corrected guided review

Keep every layout, product photo, product name, quantity, button, headline, and the entire left switch-choice panel exactly unchanged. In the right panel set PVC Pipe 1 inch to '₹245 each', PTFE tape to '₹35 each', Pipe clamp to '₹12 each', M-Seal 90g to '₹45 each', Measuring tape 5m to '₹95 each', Safety gloves to '₹60 each'. Keep switch and pipe cutter unpriced with dash. Quantities stay PVC x2, switch x2, PTFE x2, clamp x4, M-Seal x1, cutter x1, measuring tape x1, gloves x1. Right footer remains '6 items ready', 'Priced subtotal ₹808', '2 items not included'. Do not alter the three selectable switch prices ₹35, ₹65, ₹28 in the left panel. Change only those six right-panel unit-price text strings, no other edits.
